title: Who feels vulnerable to biased policing? Race, economic status and trust in Brazil
abstract: People are unevenly exposed to police stops: while some rarely experience them, others face frequent and intense encounters. This study examines perceived vulnerability to biased police interventions using nationwide survey data from Brazil and probit models. We assess whether the association between economic status and perceived vulnerability differs by race and whether race-specific income gradients exhibit different patterns across trust contexts. Higher income is consistently associated with lower perceived vulnerability among White respondents, whereas the overall income gradient among non-White respondents is substantively negligible. Economic advantage therefore does not correspond to the same reduction in perceived vulnerability across racial groups. The three-way interaction further shows different patterns across trust contexts, particularly among non-White respondents. These findings highlight racial disparities across levels of economic status and point to the need for institutional reforms addressing unequal and discretionary policing practices.
